## Result

- Skill: proposal-review
- Review status: approved
- Vision alignment: aligned
- Material findings: none
- Open blockers: none
- Proposal readiness: sufficient direction for authorized Design authoring.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop.
- Automatic downstream handoff: none.
- Claim limitations: direction approval only; no Design, deletion, implementation, proof-sufficiency, final verification, branch/PR readiness, publication or customer-adoption approval.

The exact subject is `docs/proposals/2026-09-09-consolidate-necessary-design-and-retire-superseded-sources.md` at `sha256:8bde12698a69e784b405f203c25fe8d794dcc14cc7c58759b0765543f42e2874`. The user supplied the merged direction and full text; the proposal author created the artifact and its predecessor links. The independent merged-proposal reviewer authored neither the merged contribution nor its predecessors, inspected the complete proposals, and made no proposal edits. This contribution separation supports independent approval.

## Review Dimensions

| Dimension | Judgment | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Challenge | pass | Fragmented authority and unnecessary maintained copies are material current problems. Merely moving text or deleting sources without understanding their consumers is explicitly insufficient. |
| Goals | pass | Usable current ownership, necessary engineering meaning, justified source removal and coherent consumers are outcomes. Validation supports those outcomes, and a new model is conditional. |
| Scope | pass | System/FU-012's validation-related source family bounds inspection. Exact sections belong to Design; retention and validation amendments are necessary dependencies. Distribution, Installation, Release and remaining skill adoption stay separately owned. |
| Governing principle | pass | Briefly joins necessary meaning, coherent ownership, resolved source uses and proportionate proof without selecting detailed implementation. |
| Direction | pass | Existing owners first, substantive disposition including unnumbered obligations, removal only after dependencies resolve, and coordinated consumer adoption provide a concrete decision. A new model remains available when justified. |
| Feasibility | pass | Exactly one embedded assessment has a credible existing-owner/source-family basis, bounds unresolved dependency and individual-removal questions, and does not claim savings or completed cleanup. |
| Material impact | pass | Reduced convenience of historical detail, incomplete-impact risk and scoped policy changes are disclosed alongside preservation of necessary rationale, reliance evidence and safeguards. |
| Vision alignment | pass | Necessary requirements, decisions, findings and relied-on evidence remain understandable in current artifacts. Redundant source removal does not require reconstructing current meaning from history or erase the reviewable engineering chain. |
| Downstream authority | pass | Receiving boundaries, exact amendments, removals, consumer edits, sequencing and proof allocation remain with Design, Delivery and independent assessment. Current mandatory checks cannot silently be skipped. |
| Requested decision | pass | Approves one bounded consolidation direction, explicitly rejects mandatory Validation-model/archive/broad-redesign outcomes, and preserves external-action and independent-closeout limits. |

## Scope Preservation Review

- Scope-preservation result: pass.

All material latest user goals remain explicit: necessary Design is primary; precise ownership and complete meaning are retained; consumers and dependent metadata are reconciled when affected; obsolete representation is actually removed when its remaining uses are resolved; validation is supporting and proportionate. The initial validation-related boundary survives without fixing the receiving model. The scope table's descriptive treatments unambiguously distinguish core work, same-slice dependencies and separately owned work; no extra classification table is required.

The merged decision deliberately changes the predecessor's automatic readable-original retention and predetermined Validation Execution owner. It also limits the older broad check-policy redesign to necessary amendments. Those are explicit user-selected reconciliations, not lost goals. FU-013–018 retain named receiving ownership for the excluded transfers and capability families. No separate implementation programme, new ledger or completion of those follow-ups is required here.

## Recommended Proposal Edits

- Recommended edits: none required.

## Recommendation

- Recommendation: approve this merged direction; stop after the isolated review and recording.

The proposal preserves the useful stronger transfer constraints without reintroducing the earlier conflicting outcomes. Its permission for cleanup does not itself override current retention or validation mandates: exact governing amendments must be selected and adopted before relying on changed rules. DES-SR-06/13/14/18/19 support substantive preservation, bounded ownership and coordinated consumers; TEST-SR-07–10 distinguish test usefulness from retirement and require protected boundaries; RC-SR-15 permits applicable evidence reuse while retaining freshness and independent judgment. The proposal respects those distinctions.

FU-012 currently still names a separate Validation Execution owner and preservation of existing proof policy. The latest explicit user direction and merged proposal replace that prospective selection with existing owners first and only necessary bounded amendments. It is a current consumer/follow-up item to reconcile under the selected cleanup, not a second binding proposal requirement. No change to that record or to governing policy is performed by this review.

The System inventory still uses prospective common Skill wording. Constitution's adopted Skill ownership and the prior Skill Verify explanation support inspecting that correction. This review does not renew the old Verify or independently certify its complete current dependency graph. The merged proposal accurately limits its feasibility claim and requires use of recorded completion basis before correction.

Basis inspected: complete merged proposal and both predecessor drafts; VISION.md and CONSTITUTION.md; System responsibility inventory and selected requirements; Design DES-SR-06/13/14/18/19; Test TEST-SR-07–10; Review and Closeout RC-SR-01–18; published-skill-first source context, examples, scoped retirement amendment and R1–29; FU-012–018; and prior Skill Verify's adoption explanation. These are default or triggered proposal dependencies. No-map rationale: this direction assessment uses named owners and explicit source bounds, without making an implementation dependency-graph claim. No runtime, package or benchmark execution is needed to assess a proposal that leaves exact consumer and removal decisions to inspected Design.

Current scoped CLI context, complete change registry and prior r1 review were inspected. R1 has no findings and remains stale on its original subject. The registered snapshot's old-subject drift is expected for that preserved judgment; no reliance is placed on its approval for the merged subject. There are no registered findings or blockers in the selected context. The new r2 assessment is independent of r1's conclusion and does not retarget it.

Commands used for assessment: `cat`, `sed`, `rg`; local `rigorloop context --input - --format json`; `rigorloop subject inspect --content full --format json`; `rigorloop review record --help` and the targeted `review record proposal-review-r2` operation. These establish inspected basis and recording only; no behavior-test pass or final Verify is claimed.
